From c2a16269742e176fccdd0ef9c016a233491a49ad Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Jian Shen <shenjian15@huawei.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Dec 2025 10:37:35 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] net: hns3: using the num_tqps in the vf driver to apply for
 resources

Currently, hdev->htqp is allocated using hdev->num_tqps, and kinfo->tqp
is allocated using kinfo->num_tqps. However, kinfo->num_tqps is set to
min(new_tqps, hdev->num_tqps);  Therefore, kinfo->num_tqps may be smaller
than hdev->num_tqps, which causes some hdev->htqp[i] to remain
uninitialized in hclgevf_knic_setup().

Thus, this patch allocates hdev->htqp and kinfo->tqp using hdev->num_tqps,
ensuring that the lengths of hdev->htqp and kinfo->tqp are consistent
and that all elements are properly initialized.

Fixes: e2cb1dec9779 ("net: hns3: Add HNS3 VF HCL(Hardware Compatibility Layer) Support")
Signed-off-by: Jian Shen <shenjian15@huawei.com>
Signed-off-by: Jijie Shao <shaojijie@huawei.com>
Reviewed-by: Simon Horman <horms@kernel.org>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20251211023737.2327018-2-shaojijie@huawei.com
Signed-off-by: Paolo Abeni <pabeni@redhat.com>

diff --git a/drivers/net/ethernet/hisilicon/hns3/hns3vf/hclgevf_main.c b/drivers/net/ethernet/hisilicon/hns3/hns3vf/hclgevf_main.c
index 8fcf220a120d..70327a73dee3 100644
--- a/drivers/net/ethernet/hisilicon/hns3/hns3vf/hclgevf_main.c
+++ b/drivers/net/ethernet/hisilicon/hns3/hns3vf/hclgevf_main.c
@@ -368,12 +368,12 @@ static int hclgevf_knic_setup(struct hclgevf_dev *hdev)
 	new_tqps = kinfo->rss_size * num_tc;
 	kinfo->num_tqps = min(new_tqps, hdev->num_tqps);
 
-	kinfo->tqp = devm_kcalloc(&hdev->pdev->dev, kinfo->num_tqps,
+	kinfo->tqp = devm_kcalloc(&hdev->pdev->dev, hdev->num_tqps,
 				  sizeof(struct hnae3_queue *), GFP_KERNEL);
 	if (!kinfo->tqp)
 		return -ENOMEM;
 
-	for (i = 0; i < kinfo->num_tqps; i++) {
+	for (i = 0; i < hdev->num_tqps; i++) {
 		hdev->htqp[i].q.handle = &hdev->nic;
 		hdev->htqp[i].q.tqp_index = i;
 		kinfo->tqp[i] = &hdev->htqp[i].q;
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Modifications

The patch fixes a bug in the `hclgevf_knic_setup()` function within the HNS3 VF driver (`hns3vf/hclgevf_main.c`). The issue was that `hdev->htqp` (an array of hardware transmit queue pairs) and `kinfo->tqp` (an array of pointers to those queues) were allocated and initialized with different sizes: `hdev->htqp` was allocated using `hdev->num_tqps`, while `kinfo->tqp` was allocated and initialized using `kinfo->num_tqps`. However, `kinfo->num_tqps` is set to `min(new_tqps, hdev->num_tqps)`, so it could be smaller than `hdev->num_tqps`. This caused some entries of `hdev->htqp` to remain uninitialized, leading to potential use of uninitialized memory.

### Modifications in `hclgevf_main.c`

1. **Allocation size for `kinfo->tqp`** (line 371):
   - Changed `devm_kcalloc` size from `kinfo->num_tqps` to `hdev->num_tqps`.
   - This ensures the array is allocated with the same length as `hdev->htqp`.

2. **Loop bound for initialization** (line 376):
   - Changed the loop bound from `kinfo->num_tqps` to `hdev->num_tqps`.
   - This ensures that all elements of `hdev->htqp` (and the corresponding pointers in `kinfo->tqp`) are properly initialized.

### Relationship Between the Changes

Both changes are directly related: they ensure consistency between the two arrays. The first change allocates `kinfo->tqp` with the same number of elements as `hdev->htqp`, and the second change initializes all those elements. Together, they prevent the bug where `hdev->htqp` entries beyond `kinfo->num_tqps` remained uninitialized.
